solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: On radio, Britain's leader clarified way to go

indicators.note: radio operators replace each letter with a codeword from the NATO spelling alphabet
the leader of a word is the letter standing at its front

parts.note: the first letter of Britain

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin in which the British prime minister finally sets out the route ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet B is spoken as BRAVO, the word radio users say to make the letter clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravo is a cheer of approval, the same congratulation as the exclamation 'way to go!'

clue.text: Have a host, perhaps, promoting posh European's noble deed

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, and posh is the old upper-class label U, so that letter shifts earlier in the word

parts.note: if you have a host, you are a guest: 'be a guest'
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A visitor staying with someone grand makes a gracious gesture toward an upper-class continental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' is U, the old label for upper-class usage; it is the letter promoted, moved up in front of the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Beau geste is borrowed French for a fine, magnanimous gesture, literally 'beautiful gesture'.

clue.text: Set of plans autoloads, dropping out every second

indicators.note: losing every second letter leaves only the alternate ones, first, third, fifth and so on

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters of autoloads

explanation.surface: A computer that loads programs automatically keeps skipping alternate items in a file of drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, and maps are plans of territory.

clue.text: Not allowed appropriate rank

parts.note: out means not permitted, as in 'that's out'
right means fitting or proper

explanation.surface: A forbidden promotion: an officer refused a suitable grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a noun for a grade; here it is the adjective meaning utter or complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank as an adjective means complete and unqualified, as in 'a rank amateur', the same as outright.

clue.text: Sleep-inducing, singular work, opening shortly

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
op, short for opus, is a musical work
an orifice is a hole or opening

explanation.surface: A dull one-off composition that is soon to premiere.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific is the formal adjective for anything that causes drowsiness or sends people off to sleep.

clue.text: Drive out of London area when hour is up

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' means moved higher, so the hour letter is shifted toward the top

parts.note: Soho is a district of central London

explanation.surface: A motorist leaves central London once the clock strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: H is the abbreviation for hour; it rises one place, swapping with the O above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoo is to chase away or send off, the same as to drive a creature out.

clue.text: Animated delivery worker after staff, aptly

parts.note: post is the Latin prefix meaning after, as in postwar
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk
pat as an adverb means fittingly or opportunely

explanation.surface: A cartoon courier turning up after the rest of the staff, as is fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' reads like a positional instruction, but it supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Postman Pat is the title character of a British children's stop-motion television series about a village mail carrier.

clue.text: Graduation robe rides up somewhat, as new?

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
somewhat means only a part, so the letters sit inside the run of words

parts.note: the end of graduation, all of robe and the start of rides

explanation.surface: A gown at a degree ceremony creeps up a little, looking freshly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reborn has been given new life, renewed or regenerated; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Sweet old academic keeps safe from abuse?

parts.note: a fool is a fruit-and-cream pudding

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: prof is short for professor
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An elderly professor with a sweet tooth holds on to his pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a British dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolproof describes a device so simple that misuse or mishandling cannot break it; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Fraud arising concerning programmer

parts.note: cod as a noun is a hoax or sham

indicators.note: in a down entry arising means going upward, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A scam comes to light involving a software developer.
explanation.definitionFit: A coder writes computer software, which is exactly what a programmer does.

clue.text: Washing line secured by neighbour with ten poles

indicators.note: something secured by another is held fast within it

parts.note: to neighbour is to abut, lie alongside
IO looks like the numeral 10
north and south are the two poles
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A clothes line pegged up by the people next door, propped on ten posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washing line' looks like one item, but the definition stops after 'Washing'. Ten as IO is a visual trick on the figure 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Ablutions is a formal or humorous word for washing oneself.

clue.text: Sounded disgusted, with pupil no longer returning word book

indicators.note: going back the way it came, the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: an old boy, OB, is a former pupil of a school
the Oxford English Dictionary, the great book of words

explanation.surface: A former student comes back to a dictionary and voices disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Booed means jeered with cries of disapproval, a noisy show of disgust from an audience.

clue.text: Turn to drink a little after initially extending chat

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

parts.words: drink a little after initially extending
parts.note: a small drink is a sip; its first letter is stretched to a double

explanation.surface: Someone takes a turn at the bar and prolongs the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially extending' means the opening letter of the drink is lengthened, written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk about other people, a form of casual chat.

clue.text: Not just a rascal who cheats at racing!

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
a roper is a jockey who holds back a horse to stop it winning

explanation.surface: A crooked jockey is worse than merely a scamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just' reads as 'not only' but is the definition, meaning unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper conduct is unfair or wrong, the opposite of what is just and proper.

clue.text: Judged a way to limit speed of data processing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to limit something is to put bounds around it, enclosing it

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road
bit rate measures data handled per second

explanation.surface: A referee rules on a method for capping how fast computers handle information.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee, which means judging it.

clue.text: Cut middle out of fish, eel-like?

indicators.note: taking out the middle removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: a slit is a cut
a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Gutting a fish, a cook removes its centre, finding it slippery like an eel.
explanation.definitionFit: Slithering is the sliding, snaking motion of an eel or snake; the question mark marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Yankee sits by front of treadmill, shattered after one minute

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the radio alphabet
taken as written

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of treadmill

explanation.surface: An American sits beside a running machine, exhausted after sixty seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like sixty seconds, but it is the definition, read as tiny; 'after one' puts I first.
explanation.definitionFit: Itsy-bitsy is a childish reduplicated word for very small, which is what minute means.

clue.text: Maybe seven-year itch?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lasting a great while, as seven years might be
second meaning: to yearn or crave

explanation.walkthrough: The 'seven-year itch' is the supposed restlessness after seven years of marriage; split apart, each half is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for a lengthy duration and also a verb meaning to yearn, as you might itch for something.

clue.text: Place index finger finally under peg and look for long time above

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily for a long while
T is the abbreviation for time
a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of finger

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a peg for ages and runs a finger down an index of places.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' and 'above' fix the order: the stare and the time sit above the peg and the finger's end.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazetteer is a geographical dictionary, an alphabetical index of place names.

clue.text: Looking up to notice one's lifted phone

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means raised from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one's read as 'one is', and I'm is 'I am'
to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Spotting that someone's mobile has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' suggests theft of the phone, but it reverses only the middle piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiring someone means respecting and esteeming them, which is what looking up to a person is.

clue.text: Facility allowing you to pick up tablets?

indicators.note: to pick up can mean to hear or catch a signal, so we go by sound

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so tablets are Es

explanation.surface: A pharmacy that lets you collect your pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests collecting a prescription; here it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Facility can mean effortless skill, as in 'played with facility', the same sense as ease.

clue.text: Conman in work initially filling in crack leading to slow leak briefly

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
kept brief, the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a crack player is an expert, a wizard
to ooze is to seep out slowly

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: the first letter of filling

explanation.surface: A builder fills a crack in a wall, causing a small leak to seep out.
explanation.walkthrough: In L. Frank Baum's book the Wizard turns out to be a humbug, an ordinary man faking magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wizard of Oz is the title character of a famous novel and film, who is revealed as a fraud.

clue.text: A little beef perhaps with joint

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
a hinge is a joint on which a door swings

explanation.surface: A small piece of beef cooked on the bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' and 'joint' paint a roast dinner, but beef here is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A beef is a grumble, and a whinge is a petty, whining complaint, a little one of its kind.

clue.text: Awfully brash, probing ordinary fellow's working arrangement

indicators.note: a probe goes inside something, so one piece is placed within another
done awfully, the letters are badly jumbled

parts.note: the letters of brash rearranged
Joe is the typical ordinary man, as in Joe Bloggs

explanation.surface: A tactless colleague pries into an average man's employment terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A job share is an employment arrangement where two people split one full-time post between them.

clue.text: Prize fight is broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so we go by sound

parts.note: a duel is a formal fight between two

explanation.surface: A title boxing match is being televised.
explanation.walkthrough: In many British accents duel is said 'jool', matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel is something treasured, a prize possession, as in 'the jewel of the collection'.

clue.text: Reward Tom perhaps, for waiting game

parts.note: a tip is a small cash reward
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Giving a waiter called Tom a tip for his service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reward ... for waiting' is the tip a waiter gets; tipcat is an old street game of striking a tapered wooden peg.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipcat is a traditional children's game in which a short pointed stick is flipped up and struck.

clue.text: Kid very loud following drink

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece before this word goes second

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A child gets very noisy after a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to tease them with good-humoured banter, the same as to kid.

clue.text: It's bitter, rather, outside!

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of bitter
the first and last letters of rather

explanation.surface: Someone stepping out of doors remarks that the weather is freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction and the remark a shivering person would make.
explanation.definitionFit: Brrr is the written shiver people exclaim when the weather out of doors is very cold.

clue.text: Diet once you have after Caribbean holiday?

indicators.note: the phrase reads 'what you have after', a cryptic way to define the second piece by what follows a trip

parts.note: WI stands for West Indies
a suntan is what you come back with after a sunny trip

explanation.surface: Cutting calories once you are back from a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is not about food: it is an assembly, like the Diet of Worms.
explanation.definitionFit: The witan was the Anglo-Saxon royal council, an early national assembly of the kind once called a diet.

clue.text: At home, worried, after time off

parts.note: a term is a period of time
in means at home
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Staying in, anxious, after a spell of leave from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time off' looks like a holiday, but 'off' is the definition, slang for kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To off someone is slang for killing them, and terminate is used in the same sense.

clue.text: Rare delay unsettled licensed church official

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed from its order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual hold-up has upset a parish functionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a layperson licensed by a bishop to conduct some services in the Anglican church.

clue.text: Prosper, possessing energy for a mere errand boy

indicators.note: taking possession of one letter in place of another swaps them over

parts.note: to go far is to prosper
E is the symbol for energy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Succeeding through sheer drive, though only a junior runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Energy for a' means put E in place of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer is a dogsbody who runs small errands, named from being told to 'go for' things.
